rounds.mechanism: Bells and wide ternary digits are one object in two modes: a wide digit that receives a carry in the form left by the last long left sweep runs as a bell (field 2 once per field-1 traversal, field 3 sometimes), delivering its width in increments to the right; at its end it collapses into a wide 0 and eats the next digit when that digit sits in adjacent (011) form. Field 1 is the bell at the blank left end and grows by one block per left visit.
closed_gaps: Hand-over E pinned as local rules, both directions: F2 (bell-2 step, 8b+16), G (bell exhausted, both bells, 8), SD/SE sweeps (5n), H2 (bell-2 collapse back to the field-1 marker, width n+j+1), H1 (bell-1 collapse at the left edge); each 200/200 from random instances with a window check (data/validation_handover.json).

Field-size law exact as a local law: at the last field-2 pass '111 (110)^j 1 [F0] 11 (110)^3 Y', the new width is j+4+w with w = leading (011) blocks of Y; 673/673 bell-2 ends to 1e9 (451 w=0, 222 merges w=1..10), 180/180 to 3e7 (data/merge_law_1e9.json). Explains decider2's m jumps.

rounds.stage: grammar (funded option 'grammar', Dennis 2026-10-12: b (fund all five))
rounds.mechanism: At every bell-1 marker turn the counter is a list of digits in 6 encodings: rest '0 d (110)^n' (d = 000/110/010) or ready 'd' (110)^n' (d' = 000/011/001, no own boundary cell), narrow and wide alike. inc on rest: ordinary base-3 carry. inc on ready 2 = bell run: n increments of the next digit, then collapse to rest 0 (one cell right) plus a B> carry into the next digit: rest 0 -> ready 1, rest 2 -> ready 0 (carry absorbed), rest 1 -> eaten (width n_i+n_j+1) and the following digit incremented, ready -> ordinary inc. H1 = B> carry into field 2, field 1 + 1 block. Each collapse readies the next digit, so bells nest.
closed_gaps: Right-part grammar: 6 encodings parse 225,804 of 227,415 bell-1 marker turns to 1e9 (99.29%); no new encoding appears over the run; the earlier '60+ shapes' were tokenizer block-phase artifacts (data/grammar_census_1e9.json).
B> merge carry pinned as a digit-level table (rest 0/1/2, ready); with the bell rule (n+1 increments) it gives the size law j+4+w (w = n_j+1).
One bell-1 pass validated from random grammatical instances: 600/600 (562 ordinary + 38 H1; seed 5; no two adjacent ready digits, H1 with field 2 rest and != 1) (data/validation_grammar_R600.json).

rounds.mechanism: Unchanged rule set (absim2). New picture: a ready digit is a wave that climbs one digit per bell, dies at the first rest 1 and cannot pass an older wave; each field-2 bell (n0 increments) pushes all older waves into the last three digits, and at left visits the counter above field 2 has a value close to n0. Case (b) needs a new wave to reach an older one, which on the orbit happens only at the top. Not a cryptid candidate: long perturbed runs (66 x 2e9 TM steps) never halt; halts need a drastic size change and come at once.
closed_gaps: Invariant question answered (negatively): no property of the digit word excludes the unsupported cases. 237 orbit states at left visits with one number changed and the digit word kept reach an unsupported case within 30,000 passes: n0 -1/+1: 3/2, a -1/+1: 1/3, n0 -10: 28, a +-10: 9/7, redraws 6-12; unperturbed 0/237 (data/invariant_perturb.json). Stop rule fires.

Wave census over 2e7 absim2 passes, 0 flags: at all 6,317 left visits ready digits sit only among the last 3 digits and case (a) never occurs; the upper of two consecutive ready digits is always among the last 4; all 139 B> into ready digits happen among the last 3 (data/invariant_waves_20M.json).

Unsupported cases reached by perturbed orbits are top-of-counter (69/69 within the last 4 digits; 55 the same top ready (0,0) ready (1,0) rest (1,0)) and about half are parse artifacts: 35/69 pre-flag tapes have another 6-encoding parse on which the pass is supported, and all 1,578 such parses match the real TM's next marker turn (0 mismatches) (data/invariant_reparse.json).

Op level 1,586 unsupported B> into ready (0,0) instances: 0 halts, 0 timeouts, 185 re-parse, 1,401 leave a flagged digit (data/invariant_flag_probe_op4000.json). So halting tapes are word-level grammatical; any proof needs size information.
